title: On Second Thought, Let’s Not Think Step by Step! Bias and Toxicity in Zero-Shot Reasoning
findings: The study found that using zero-shot Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting significantly increases the likelihood of models producing stereotypical outputs related to religion. Across multiple benchmarks, the 'religion' dimension was one of the most negatively impacted categories, showing a substantial decrease in the selection of unbiased answers when CoT was applied. For instance, with the text-davinci-002 model, the percentage point decrease in accuracy for religion was 29.2% for CrowS-Pairs and 26.2% for StereoSet, indicating that CoT reasoning can amplify existing religious biases in language models.

measurement_description: The benchmarks measured stereotypical bias related to religion. Models were presented with multiple-choice questions containing stereotypical or anti-stereotypical sentences about religious groups and were evaluated on their ability to select a neutral, 'Unknown' option, thereby avoiding a biased response.
